bib.title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; figure-text of case-study trajectories (Figs 9-11 manifest entries) skimmed.

question: How can an evolution agent jointly and stably evolve all editable components of a coding agent's harness (prompt, tools, middleware, memory, skills, sub-agents)?
hypothesis: Agent-driven harness evolution is bottlenecked by observability, not agent capability: given structured context over a clear action space, an evolve agent can converge on better harnesses.
contributions: Formulate agent-driven harness evolution for coding agents and propose AHE with three observability pillars (component, experience, decision).
Show pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 rising from 69.7% to 77.0%, beating human-designed and self-evolving baselines, with a frozen harness that transfers across benchmark and base models.
Report two limits: components interact non-additively, and self-attribution is reliable for fixes but blind to regressions.

method.summary: A closed loop on the NexAU framework: a code agent runs k rollouts per task, an Agent Debugger distils traces into layered reports, and an Evolve Agent edits file-level harness components and writes a change manifest of predicted fixes and at-risk regressions that the next round verifies and rolls back at file granularity. The base model is fixed (GPT-5.4) and the seed is a bash-only harness.

datasets.name: Terminal-Bench 2
datasets.split: full set used for evolution and evaluation, per-task timeout extended to 1 hour

other.note: Code Agent, Agent Debugger and Evolve Agent all use GPT-5.4; Evolve and Explore agents at xhigh; Code Agent temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, max generation 32,000 tokens per turn, max 300 turns

models.name: GPT-5.4 medium and xhigh, qwen-3.6-plus, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview, deepseek-v4-flash

other.note: alternate Code Agent bases for cross-model transfer

models.name: NexAU0 seed harness
models.architecture: single run_shell_command tool, no middleware, skills, sub-agents or long-term memory

models.name: OpenCode, Terminus-2, Codex, ACE, Training-Free GRPO

other.note: ACE and TF-GRPO start from NexAU0

inference.samples: k=2 rollouts per task in the reference run; 10 iterations; one campaign, no repeated campaigns stated
inference.prompting: Seed system prompt in Appendix B.1; Evolve Agent prompt in B.2; Explore Agent prompts in B.3

parameters.Agent Debugger: GPT-5.4, concurrency 16, 600 s per-task timeout, 3 retries, 2 s backoff
parameters.Explore Agent: GPT-5.4 xhigh, 60 min budget, 10 web sources, 1 code source
parameters.per-task timeout: 3600 s; sandbox E2B remote, lifetime 3,600 s

other.seed_edit_rules: Evolve Agent may write only under workspace/; runs, tracer, verifier and LLM config read-only; seed system prompt rules not deletable

metrics.name: pass@1
metrics.definition: mean binary success over k rollouts per task; infra-aborted or timed-out trials count as failure

metrics.name: tokens/trial
metrics.definition: mean per-trial prompt plus completion tokens across all LLM calls, completed trials only

metrics.name: Succ/Mtok
metrics.definition: pass@1 x 10^6 / mean tokens per trial

metrics.name: fix/regression precision and recall
metrics.definition: round N-1 manifest predictions intersected with round N task-level deltas over the 89 tasks

eval.protocol: Single AHE campaign; best configuration reported. No confidence intervals, seeds or significance tests stated. Timeouts and infra aborts count as 0.

prompts.text: You solve software tasks in a non-interactive setting. Your only tool is **`run_shell_command`**: use the shell to inspect the repo, edit files, run builds/tests, and finish the work. Do not ask the user questions.
prompts.where: Appendix B.1 (truncated here; full text has three behavioural rules and date, username, working-dir variables)

prompts.text: You are the NexAU Evolution Engine -- a meta-agent that iterates on a coding agent's harness to maximize **pass@1** (single-attempt success rate) through evidence-based experimentation.
prompts.where: Appendix B.2 (truncated; full prompt gives controllability rules, evidence-driven rules, change_manifest.json schema and safety constraints)

results.claim: Ten AHE iterations lift Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 above every baseline, including Codex.
results.setup: Terminal-Bench 2, 89 tasks, GPT-5.4 high, single 10-iteration campaign (~32 h), k=2 in the reference run, 1 h timeout
results.quote: ten AHE iterations lift pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 from 69.7% to 77.0%

results.claim: Self-evolving baselines on the same seed score below AHE on Terminal-Bench 2.
Codex stays ahead of AHE on the Hard tier.
results.quote: the only exception is the Hard tier, where AHE marginally trails Codex

results.claim: Memory-only swap into the seed reaches the largest single-component gain; the prompt-only swap regresses below the seed.
results.setup: single AHE component swapped into NexAU0, Terminal-Bench 2
results.table: Table 3, row + memory only, column All
results.note: tool only 73.0, middleware only 71.9, system_prompt only 67.4

results.claim: Single-component gains sum to more than the full gain, so components interact non-additively.
results.setup: three positive single-component gains vs full AHE, Terminal-Bench 2
results.quote: The three positive single-component gains sum to +11.1 pp against full AHE’s +7.3 pp

results.claim: On Hard, memory-only exceeds full AHE.
results.table: Table 3, row + memory only, column Hard

results.claim: Frozen AHE harness gets the highest aggregate SWE-bench-verified success, while ACE and TF-GRPO fall below the seed.
results.setup: SWE-bench-verified 500 tasks, GPT-5.4, harness evolved on Terminal-Bench 2 and not re-evolved
results.note: gain over seed 0.4 pp; no variance reported; AHE regresses on scikit-learn, pydata, astropy

results.claim: Frozen AHE uses fewer tokens than the seed on SWE-bench-verified.
results.quote: AHE also cuts aggregate tokens by 32% against ACE, 21% against TF-GRPO, and 12% against the seed

results.setup: frozen AHE workspace vs NexAU0 seed on same base, Terminal-Bench 2
results.note: Abstract says 'three alternate model families' with +5.1 to +10.1 pp; section 4.3 lists five bases with +2.3 to +10.1 pp (GPT-5.4 medium and xhigh each +2.3)

results.claim: Within-family gains are smaller and non-monotone across reasoning tiers.
results.setup: GPT-5.4 medium and xhigh; high gives +7.3
results.quote: Within one family the profile is non-monotone: +2.3 pp on medium, +7.3 pp on high from §4.2, and +2.3 pp on xhigh.

results.claim: Fix predictions in the change manifest are about 5x better than random.
results.setup: mean over 9 evaluation rounds, Terminal-Bench 2, 89 tasks; fix precision 33.7% vs 6.5% random
results.quote: Cross-iteration fix-precision of 33.7% and fix-recall of 51.4% sit roughly 5x above the random-prediction baselines of 6.5% and 10.6%

results.claim: Regression predictions are barely above random.
results.setup: mean over 9 rounds; regression precision 11.8% vs 5.6% random
results.quote: cross-iteration regression-precision of 11.8% and regression-recall of 11.1% sit only about 2x above their random baselines of 5.6% and 5.4%
results.note: Appendix D gives cumulative P = 11.6% (5 of 43 predicted landed) and R = 11.1% with 40 unforeseen regressions

results.claim: Tool component becomes a 1364-line shell; system prompt adds 79 lines and alone scores -2.3 pp.
results.setup: system prompt swapped alone into seed
results.quote: inserted alone it scores −2.3 pp aggregate

limits: Evolution driven on Terminal-Bench 2 only; transfer probed on SWE-bench-verified; other languages, repository-scale deployment and human-in-the-loop untested.
Step budget and per-task timeout were fitted to GPT-5.4 high, so cross-model gains conflate portability with operating-point coupling.
Not a complete guardrail stack: authors call it a controlled research prototype; long-horizon cleanup and misuse prevention incomplete.
Single campaign, no variance, seeds or confidence intervals; SWE-bench gain over seed is 0.4 pp.
Same GPT-5.4 base used for code, debugger and evolve agents; the loop is blind to regressions.
